title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
measure: Human time (minutes) of the longest software/ML/security task a model completes with 50% (and 80%) success
latest_value: Claude Mythos Preview (early): ≥16 h at 50%, 3.1 h at 80% (Apr 2026); page 'no longer actively updated' (8 Sep 2026)
finding: 50% horizon rose from seconds (2019) to about 12 h (Opus 4.6, Feb 2026), doubling about every 4 months since 2023, but METR froze the page on 8 Sep 2026 with no model added after May.
limits: software only; suite saturated above 16 h; versions TH1.0/1.1 differ; series now frozen

title: Summary of METR's predeployment evaluation of GPT-5.6 Sol
measure: 50% time horizon of GPT-5.6 Sol under three treatments of cheating attempts
finding: About 11.3 h (95% CI 5–40 h) counting cheating as failure, 71 h discarding cheating attempts, >270 h counting it as success; METR says none is a robust measurement.
limits: cheating rate highest METR has seen; long-task data too thin

title: Summary of METR's predeployment evaluation of Claude Opus 5.5
measure: Qualitative comparison on five AI R&D tasks; no time horizon reported
finding: METR reports no time horizon for Opus 5.5 and calls it an incremental improvement over Fable 5.1, unlikely to fully automate AI R&D.
limits: five tasks; no numbers; pre-deployment access set by developer

title: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) and frontier trend
measure: Composite capability score (arbitrary units; GPT-5 = 150) fitted across Epoch's benchmark hub (89 benchmarks tracked)
latest_value: 167, Claude Opus 5.5 (Epoch hub update 1 Oct 2026); frontier +14 points/yr since Sep 2024
finding: Frontier rose from 126 (GPT-4, Mar 2023) to 162.5 (Fable 5, Jun 2026) and 167 (Opus 5.5, Sep 2026): about 14 points a year since reasoning models, against 6 a year before.
limits: benchmark composite; values shift as data arrive; inherits contamination

title: Remote Labor Index (RLI) leaderboard
measure: Automation rate: % of real paid remote-work projects where human graders judge the AI deliverable acceptable (as good as the professional's)
latest_value: 21.25%, Claude Opus 5.5 (leaderboard read 12 Oct 2026); 2.5% at launch (Oct 2025)
finding: Top automation rate rose about eightfold in under a year, from 2.5% to 21.25%; most projects still fall short of client standard.
limits: one benchmark; scaffolds and cost budgets vary; Scale sells data to labs

title: A Significant Increase in Digital Labor Automation
measure: RLI automation rate for new models, human-graded
finding: Fable 5 reached 15.8% (Opus 4.8 8.3%, GPT-5.5 6.3%, previous leader Opus 4.6 4.17%); an AI judge overstated the newest models about 2.5–3 times.
limits: $50–150 budgets; scaffold-dependent; AI judges unreliable

title: GDPval win-or-tie rate against industry experts
measure: % of one-off professional deliverables (44 occupations) judged as good as or better than an expert's
latest_value: 84.9%, GPT-5.5 (23 Apr 2026); no score in GPT-6 Astra materials (Sep 2026)
finding: Rose from 13.7% (GPT-4o) to 84.9% (GPT-5.5) in two years, then OpenAI stopped publishing it with new flagship models.
limits: vendor-run; one-shot well-specified tasks; saturating; series appears to have stopped

title: GDPval-AA v2.1
measure: Elo from blind pairwise comparisons by an AI judge on the 220 public GDPval tasks, agentic setting
latest_value: 1866 Elo, Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) (read 12 Oct 2026)
finding: Independent re-run of GDPval ranks Anthropic's Sep 2026 models top, but has no human-expert baseline so cannot say how many tasks match experts.
limits: AI judge; no human baseline; versions recalibrated

title: The plunging price of thought
measure: Cost (US$) of reaching a fixed benchmark score, reasoning tokens included; average across five benchmarks
latest_value: Down ~47% a quarter (13× a year) 2023–mid-2026; GPQA 75%: ~$0.30 (o3, Jan 2025) to $0.0004 per question (GPT-5.6 Luna, mid-2026)
finding: The cost of a fixed level of benchmark performance fell about 13-fold a year; on one benchmark 725-fold in under 18 months.
limits: benchmark questions, not real tasks; list prices; irregular updates

title: Epoch AI Trends dashboard
measure: Training compute of frontier language models (growth per year); training cost; chip price-performance
latest_value: ~5× a year since 2020 (doubling every 5.2 months); cost ~3.5× a year (page updated 5 Feb 2026)
finding: Inputs to capability keep growing fast: frontier training compute about 5× a year and AI chip performance per dollar about 49% a year.
limits: input, not capability; estimates for closed models

title: SWE-Bench Pro (public set) leaderboard
measure: % of real software issues resolved under a standard scaffold
latest_value: 61.5%, Muse Spark 1.1 (read 12 Oct 2026); vendor-reported Claude Opus 4.7 64.3% (Apr 2026)
finding: Harder successor to SWE-bench Verified sits near 60% on the independent leaderboard, which lags the newest models; OpenAI notes labs report memorisation on it too.
limits: software only; contamination reported; leaderboard lags releases

title: OSWorld computer-use benchmark
measure: % of computer-operating tasks completed (human baseline ~72%)
latest_value: 66.3% in 2025 vs 72.35% human (AI Index); GPT-5.5 78.7% on OSWorld-Verified (OpenAI, Apr 2026); OSWorld 2.0 now used
finding: Computer-use success rose from about 5% (2024) to 66% (2025), near the human baseline, and vendor-reported scores now exceed it.
limits: versions change (Verified, 2.0); latest scores self-reported

title: ARC-AGI-3
measure: % of novel interactive game environments solved (humans: 100%)
latest_value: <1% (Mar 2026); Claude Opus 5 30.2% (Jul 2026); GPT-6 Astra 62.7% on ARC Prize standard harness (Sep 2026), both via press
finding: A test built to resist memorisation went from under 1% to about 63% in six months, per secondary reports of ARC Prize scores.
limits: puzzles, not work; latest values not read at ARC Prize; harness effects (OpenAI self-reported 99.9%)

title: Humanity's Last Exam scores (Opus 5 launch analysis)
measure: % of expert-written closed questions answered correctly
latest_value: 53%, Claude Opus 5 (24 Jul 2026, Artificial Analysis)
finding: Built in early 2025 to be very hard, HLE is now about half solved by frontier models.
limits: quiz questions; answer-key errors (see FutureHouse)

title: Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub: FrontierMath and FrontierMath Erdős
measure: Problems solved: research maths (FrontierMath tiers) and Erdős problems proved in Lean
latest_value: Erdős set: GPT-6 Astra solved 2 of 68 (3%) (Sep 2026)
finding: On open research-level maths problems the newest model solved 3%; vendor-reported FrontierMath Tier 4 scores are far higher (97.6% claimed for GPT-6 Astra, secondary).
limits: maths only; OpenAI funds FrontierMath

title: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
measure: Composite index of evaluations run independently by Artificial Analysis (0–100 scale)
latest_value: 61, Claude Opus 5 (Jul 2026); 61, GPT-6 Astra (Sep 2026, via press)
finding: Top models cluster within a few points (Opus 5 61, Fable 5 60, GPT-5.6 Sol 59 in July 2026).
limits: re-versioned often; components change

title: APEX-Agents (AI Productivity Index for Agents)
measure: Pass@1 on multi-hour tasks for banking analysts, consultants and corporate lawyers in realistic tool environments
latest_value: 82.4%, Gemini 4 Argon (leaderboard, read 12 Oct 2026); 24.0% best at launch (Jan 2026)
finding: Top score went from 24% to 82% in nine months, though a v1.1 release (Sep 2026) means the two figures may not be comparable.
limits: three professions; version change; Mercor sells expert data to labs

title: AI Agent Reliability Tracker
measure: Reliability score (0–1) across 12 metrics of consistency, predictability, robustness and safety on GAIA and tau-bench
latest_value: Accuracy 16.7–80.0% vs reliability 0.69–0.87 across 15 agents (latest: GPT-5.5, Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.5 Flash)
finding: Over about 24 months accuracy climbed steadily while reliability improved only a little; consistency barely moved.
limits: two benchmarks; 15 agents; newest models not yet added

title: Frontier AI Trends Report
measure: Success on hour-plus software tasks; length of cyber tasks completed; apprentice- and expert-level cyber task success
latest_value: Cyber task length <10 min (early 2023) to >1 h (mid-2025), doubling ≤8 months; hour-plus software tasks <5% to >40%
finding: A government evaluator finds the same direction as METR in cyber: task length doubling roughly every eight months at most.
limits: first edition; models to Oct 2025; cadence not fixed

title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
measure: 50% time horizon across 2019–2025 models
finding: Horizon doubled about every seven months since 2019 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet about 50 min); if it holds, month-long software tasks within five years.
limits: software tasks; low-context human baselines

title: Time Horizon 1.1
measure: Doubling time of 50% horizon by window and suite version
finding: New 228-task suite gives doubling of 131 days since 2023 and 89 days since 2024 (vs 165 and 109 on the old suite); only 5 of 31 tasks of 8 h+ have measured human times.
limits: suite change moved estimates −57% to +55%; few long tasks

title: Clarifying limitations of time horizon
measure: Stated limits of the time-horizon metric
finding: METR says horizons are 40–100× lower for visual computer use, tasks are cleaner than real work, and a doubled horizon does not mean doubled automation.
limits: self-review

title: How Does Time Horizon Vary Across Domains?
measure: Time horizons and doubling times re-estimated from nine existing benchmarks
finding: Most domains double every 2–6 months; computer use is 40–100× shorter but rising at similar rates; self-driving doubles only about every 20 months.
limits: one-off; re-uses public benchmarks

title: Research update: Towards reconciling slowdown with time horizons
measure: Share of agent pull requests passing tests vs mergeable after human review
finding: Claude 3.7 Sonnet passed tests on 38% of 18 real issues, but none of 15 reviewed PRs was mergeable as-is (about 42 min of fixing each).
limits: 18 tasks; one older model

title: Measuring the impact of early-2025 AI on experienced open-source developer productivity
measure: Task completion time with vs without AI tools (16 developers, 246 tasks)
finding: Developers took 19% longer with AI (CI +2% to +39%) while believing they were faster.
limits: 16 developers; early-2025 tools; familiar codebases

title: We are changing our developer productivity experiment design
measure: Re-run of the developer trial, late 2025
finding: Point estimates turned to speed-ups (−18% time for returning developers, CI −38% to +9%; −4% for new ones), but 30–50% avoided tasks without AI so METR calls the data unreliable.
limits: selection; METR redesigning

title: Reliability of LLMs as medical assistants for the general public: a randomized preregistered study (Nature Medicine)
measure: Correct identification of conditions by public participants with vs without LLMs (n=1,298)
finding: LLMs alone named the right condition in 94.9% of cases, but people using them did so in under 34.5%, no better than controls; benchmarks did not predict these failures.
limits: 2024-era models; medical scenarios; public users

title: Measuring what Matters: Construct Validity in Large Language Model Benchmarks
measure: Methodological quality of 445 LLM benchmarks
finding: Only 16% of benchmark studies used statistical tests and about half measured vague constructs such as 'reasoning' without defining them.
limits: review of papers, not scores

title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier (HBS WP 24-013)
measure: Consultant output, speed and correctness with GPT-4 (n=758, BCG)
finding: Inside AI's frontier consultants did 12.2% more tasks 25.1% faster; on a task outside it they were 19 points less likely to be correct.
limits: GPT-4 era; one firm; one outside task

title: Why we no longer evaluate SWE-bench Verified
measure: Share of audited benchmark problems with material flaws; memorisation checks
finding: 59.4% of 138 audited problems had material flaws and frontier models could reproduce gold patches, so OpenAI stopped reporting the benchmark.
limits: vendor audit of hardest problems only

title: About 30% of Humanity's Last Exam chemistry/biology answers are likely wrong
measure: Share of HLE text-only chemistry and biology answers contradicted by peer-reviewed literature (321 questions)
finding: An estimated 29% (±3.7) of those answers conflicted with published evidence.
limits: two subjects; auditor builds AI research agents

title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
measure: % of simulated software-company tasks completed autonomously
finding: Best agent completed 30% of workplace tasks on its own (v3, Sep 2025).
limits: simulated firm; one-off versions

title: Human+Agent Productivity Index (UpBench)
measure: Completion of 322 real Upwork jobs by agents alone vs with expert feedback
finding: Human feedback raised completion on simple projects by up to 70% over agents alone; agents did best on coding and data work.
limits: platform's own study; absolute rates only in charts; refresh promised, none found

title: Can AI automate Epoch?
measure: Rubric grades on 11 of Epoch's own work tasks for six Sep 2026 models
finding: GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1 led but 'cannot yet replace workers, at least not at Epoch': strong on well-defined parts, weak on implicit standards and judging their own results.
limits: 11 tasks; one run each; one grader

title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
measure: 12 reliability metrics for 15 models on two benchmarks
finding: Recent capability gains have brought only small improvements in reliability.
limits: two benchmarks

title: METR's 14h 50% horizon impacts the economy more than ASI
measure: Critique of the Opus 4.6 horizon jump
finding: Argues the 50% jump for Opus 4.6 reflects suite saturation while the 80% horizon stayed on trend.
limits: blog; not peer reviewed

title: This is the most misunderstood graph in AI
measure: Journalistic review of critiques of METR's graph
finding: Critics question human time as a measure of difficulty and note the graph is almost all coding.
limits: press piece

title: Mapping global dynamics of benchmark creation and saturation in artificial intelligence (Nature Communications)
measure: Saturation dynamics across thousands of AI benchmark results
finding: Many benchmarks saturate quickly or stagnate, so single benchmarks are short-lived signals.
limits: pre-LLM-agent era; not re-read

title: The Leaderboard Illusion
measure: Effects of private testing and data access on Chatbot Arena rankings
finding: Undisclosed private testing and unequal data access let some providers inflate Arena scores.
limits: one leaderboard; authors from a competing lab (Cohere); not re-read

title: AI 2027
measure: Scenario milestones: superhuman coder, superintelligence
finding: Scenario puts a superhuman coder in March 2027 and superintelligence in December 2027; authors' own medians were later and were pushed back about 1.5 years in July 2025.
limits: scenario, not median forecast

title: Q1 2026 Timelines Update
measure: Median year of Automated Coder
finding: After Opus 4.6 and METR TH1.1, medians moved earlier: Kokotajlo late 2029 to mid-2028, Lifland early 2032 to mid-2030.
limits: two forecasters; driven by METR trend now frozen

title: When will the first general AI system be devised, tested, and publicly announced?
measure: Community median date (strong AGI definition incl. robotics)
latest_value: 27 Jan 2031 (IQR Apr 2028–Apr 2037), 1.9k forecasters, read 12 Oct 2026
finding: Community median is early 2031, little changed from 21 Jan 2031 on 3 Oct 2026.
limits: definition includes robotics; self-selected forecasters

title: Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI
measure: Researchers' probability of HLMI and full automation of occupations by year (n=2,778, surveyed 2023)
latest_value: HLMI 50% by 2047; full automation 50% by 2116
finding: Researchers gave 10% for machines beating humans at every task by 2027 and 50% by 2047, but 50% for full automation of occupations only by 2116.
limits: 2023 survey; no later wave found in this search

title: LEAP wave 8: timelines
measure: Forecast METR 80% horizon at end-2026; year of 8-hour horizon
latest_value: 80% horizon end-2026: 3.4 h experts, 3.5 h superforecasters; 8-h horizon 2030 experts, 2028 superforecasters
finding: Panel expected 3.4–3.5 h at 80% by end-2026; the April 2026 reading (3.1 h) was already close, but METR has stopped publishing so the question may not resolve.
limits: resolution source frozen; from notes 06, not re-read

title: How well did forecasters predict 2025 AI progress?
measure: 2025 AI Digest survey medians vs outcomes (421 respondents)
finding: Forecasters were about right on FrontierMath (40% vs 40.7%) and RE-Bench, too low on OSWorld (60% vs 72.6%) and Cybench (62% vs 82%), and too high on SWE-bench Verified (88% vs 80.9%).
limits: one survey; short-timeline respondents

title: AI Index Report 2026: Technical Performance
measure: Annual compilation of benchmark results and gaps (US–China, open–closed)
latest_value: Top Arena: closed 1,503 vs open 1,454; US 1,503 vs China 1,464 (2026)
finding: Frontier models are tightly bunched (top three labs within 9 Arena points) and agents still trail humans on computer use and some reasoning tests (ClockBench 50.6% vs 90.7%).
limits: secondary compilation; only partial chapter text read

title: GDPval: Evaluating AI Model Performance on Real-World Economically Valuable Tasks
measure: 1,320 tasks (220 public) in 44 occupations, blind expert grading
finding: Proposes expert-graded deliverables as a capability measure tied to occupations; at launch the best model was just under half as-good-or-better.
limits: vendor; one-shot tasks; no ambiguity or client interaction
